adjudication_label: batch_2:Refractory High-Entropy Alloy processing variables for strength
canonical_question: What specific processing variables (e.g., powder size, sintering pressure) enabled the 1542 MPa fracture strength compared to the 1010 MPa of the as-cast alloy?

question_variants.question: What specific processing variables (e.g., powder size, sintering pressure) enabled the 1542 MPa fracture strength compared to the 1010 MPa of the as-cast alloy?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper specifies the processing variables used for the composite (SPS at 30 MPa, 1700 C, 30 min) and mentions ball milling. It states the strength increased from 1010 MPa (as-cast) to 1542 MPa. It does not explicitly detail the exact variables that *specifically* caused the jump (e.g., isolating sintering pressure vs. carbide content vs. grain refinement) beyond the general statement that the P/M method with carbides/oxides was developed to increase strength.

answers.answer: The composite was processed by high energy planetary ball milling (39 h, 300 rpm, argon) followed by SPS consolidation (30 MPa, 1700 C, 30 min). The text states the fracture strength increased to 1542 MPa compared to 1010 MPa for the as-cast alloy, attributing the improvement to the development of the P/M composite with dispersed carbides and oxides.
answers.conditions: SPS 30 MPa, 1700 C; Ball milling 300 rpm
answers.mechanism: Dispersion strengthening from in-situ carbides/oxides; grain refinement from P/M
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific contribution of individual variables (e.g., pressure alone) to the strength increase is not quantified in the text
evidence_spans: Powders of Nb, Mo, Cr, Ti, and Al with purity higher than 99.5 wt. % and particle size of ≤45 μm were used as starting materials.
The elemental powder was mixed in equiatomic composition and then processed by high energy planetary ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm in a pure argon atmosphere (YXQM-2L, MITR, Changsha, China).
Tungsten carbide vials and balls were utilized as the milling media with a ball-to-powder ratio of 10:1.

source_evidence_spans: the fracture strength of the composite was 1542 MPa, increasing by more than a half than that of the as-cast alloy (1010 MPa)
